headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: AutoGen can execute code and write files while next-ai-draw-io ingests MCP/API-driven document content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute code, while next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and browser/API-driven document processing. If AutoGen consumes next-ai-draw-io outputs from a shared workspace or copied files, attacker-controlled document text can steer instructions. The shared channel is not explicit, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory or exchanged files
IF next-ai-draw-io output is fed into AutoGen without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated documents
Add provenance tags to exchanged files
Review any copied text before AutoGen tool use
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization gates

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, and next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams through external model APIs. A shared workspace or copied files could expose sensitive application data to the second agent’s outbound calls. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are available to both agents
IF next-ai-draw-io sends those files to a remote model provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use local-only models for next-ai-draw-io
Redact secrets before document upload
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress, browser use, and MCP. Even without explicit shared locks, overlapping mutable surfaces create conflict risk if both operate on the same files or external resources. Because shared state is developer-defined, the interaction is plausible but not guaranteed.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same directory or diagram artifacts
IF both agents act on the same external MCP-backed resource
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths
Serialize writes with a lock file
Avoid concurrent edits to the same diagram
Use read-only copies for one agent
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code and act through tools, while next-ai-draw-io performs AI-assisted visualization and can call external models. If AutoGen-produced text or facts are treated as authoritative input to next-ai-draw-io, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io renders or acts on AutoGen output without verification
IF AutoGen output is used as source material for diagrams or prompts
mitigations: Require human review before downstream use
Add a verification step between agents
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted
Limit next-ai-draw-io to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for exchanged artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and broad network egress; next-ai-draw-io sends document content to multiple external AI providers and handles PDFs, text, images, and diagrams. If regulated or sensitive documents are processed, residency and retention obligations can diverge across providers. The profiles do not specify certifications, so this is a compliance-risk medium, not high.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed through next-ai-draw-io
IF the configured model provider stores or transfers data outside required jurisdictions
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive data
Choose providers with matching residency terms
Disable retention where available
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: add policy-based provider routing
